title: How to install npm
content:
Npm (Node Package Manager) is a popular package manager for JavaScript projects. It allows you to easily install and manage dependencies for your Node.js applications. Here are the steps to install npm:

  1. Install Node.js: Npm comes bundled with Node.js, so you need to install Node.js first. Visit the official Node.js website (https://nodejs.org) and download the latest stable version for your operating system. Run the installer and follow the instructions to complete the installation.
  2. Verify Installation: After installing Node.js, open a command prompt or terminal and type the following command to check if Node.js and npm are installed successfully: 
    node -v
    npm -v
    If the versions are displayed, it means Node.js and npm are installed correctly.
  3. Update npm (optional): npm gets updated frequently with new features and bug fixes. To update npm to the latest version, use the following command: 
    npm install -g npm@latest
    The -g flag ensures that npm is installed globally on your system.
  4. Start Using npm: Once npm is installed, you can start using it to manage your JavaScript dependencies in your projects. Navigate to your project's directory using the command prompt or terminal, and use npm commands such as npm install to install packages listed in your project's package.json file.

That's it! You have successfully installed npm on your system and are ready to manage your JavaScript project dependencies using npm.
